errors.text: The proposed critical threshold of approximately 500–600 K conflicts with the target finding that substantial diffusion, segregation, and stability loss become dominant above approximately 673 K.
The heating protocol stops at 800 K and therefore cannot reproduce the decisive Au/Cu-shell melting and evaporation observed at 973 K.
The cited studies concern materially different bulk or refractory high-entropy systems and do not directly support Au/Cu surface segregation or diffusion kinetics in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
